Who signs in, which roles exist, and what each role may read and change. **Preview** keys work and may change in any release ([status](/docs/status/)); the rest are stable. [All parts](/docs/app-dsl/).

```ts
auth: {
  providers: ['email'],
  defaultRole: 'viewer',
  roles: {
    viewer: { label: 'Viewer', read: true },
    manager: { label: 'Manager', read: true, write: ['opportunity'], commands: ['assignReviewer'], operations: ['readiness'] },
  },
},
```

Present, every request needs a session. A role takes a `label` for people,
`read` (`true` or a list), `write` (within its reads), `commands` (command
ids), `actions` (`{ pay_run: ['approve'] }`: fixed actions without write),
`operations`, `fields` and, from an identity provider, `from` (the claims that
grant it). Omitted grants deny, and every grant is enforced by the server, not
the screen. An account holding `admin` manages accounts from the account menu.
See [Sign-in](/docs/sign-in/), [Roles and field access](/docs/roles/) and
[Row access](/docs/row-access/).

`store` is where accounts and sessions live: a SQLite file in the config
directory by default, or a dedicated PostgreSQL database by its `postgres://`
URL. The manifest is committed, so name the password, or the whole URL, by a
`${NAME}` reference (`store: '${MISTRI_AUTH_STORE}'`); an unset variable
refuses at startup. Run `migratePostgresAuthStore(url)` from
`@mistriwork/mistri/maintenance` once before the first start: startup checks the store's
schema and never creates it. The store is never a business database, and a
tenant App refuses one at startup ([Tenant Apps](/docs/tenant-apps/)).

## `auth`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth` | object | Stable | Sign-in for this App, through Better Auth. Present, every request needs a session. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |

## `auth.challenge`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.challenge` | string | Stable | The human check every public door asks before it reads a submission: the name of a verifier the commands module exports in challenges (defineChallenges from @mistriwork/mistri/commands). |

## `auth.defaultRole`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.defaultRole` | string | Stable | The role a new account gets. Default: user. |

## `auth.me`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.me` | object | Stable | Who me is as a row: the table people are rows of and its column holding their sign-in email, so owner_id = me compares a reference to that table with the signed-in person's row. Without it, me is the account's email and compares with text columns only. In a tenant App column holds the account's id, and me is the row of the tenant the request is in; a tenant with no row for them matches nothing. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.me.column` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.me.create` | object | Stable | Make each new account's row the first time it is signed in to the App: its email in column (which must be unique) and, where name names a column, its name there. Every other column the row needs must have a default. Not in a tenant App yet. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.me.create.name` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `auth.me.from` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |

## `auth.roles`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.roles` | object | Stable | Grants within the resource ceilings. Needs at least one resources.&lt;r>.access; omitted grants deny. |
| `auth.roles.*.actions` | object | Stable | Fixed actions the role runs without write, by resource and action id: { pay_run: ['submit'] }. Each resource is one the role reads, with access 'write', and does not write; each id is one of its fixed (set) actions. The server admits the update only as that action: its set, its reason column, its when on the stored row. Needs auth.rows 'all'. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.claims` | object | Stable | The identity provider's claims that give this role: { &lt;claim, or a dotted path into one>: [values] }, and optionally provider, the one provider they are read from. Re-read at every sign-in; not in a tenant App. |
| `auth.roles.*.claims.provider` | string | Stable | The one named identity provider whose claims these are, oidc('workforce') or saml('corp'): a sign-in through another never reads the rule. Without it any of the App's providers does, and check warns where there are several. |
| `auth.roles.*.commands` | array | Stable | Explicit server command identifiers only. No wildcard grants or implied CRUD access. Default `[]`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.create` | array | Stable | Of what the role writes, what it makes new records in. Absent: everything it writes. false: it edits and never creates (no New, quick add or related add, and the server refuses the insert). A list names the few it creates. One of `false`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.experiments` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.experiments[].actions` | array | Preview |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.experiments[].environments` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.experiments[].ids` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.experiments[].owners` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.export` | array | Stable | Tables the role may export (the whole matching list as a CSV or JSON file) beyond those it writes, which it always may. Of what it reads. A signed-out visitor never may. An App without role grants keeps its one switch, ui.export. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.extends` | string | Stable | Another role whose grants this one holds too: { manager: { extends: 'mechanic', commands: ['approveQuote'] } }. A chain is followed; a loop is refused. Only grants pass down, each the union of both; never label, claims or service, and only within one realm. A view's or page's roles open to a role that extends one they name; a row policy's principal.roles still match by name. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.fields` | object | Stable | Column narrowing per resource, within the resource's own fields. Omit read to narrow only write. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.fields.*.read` | array | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.fields.*.write` | array | Stable | Needs the resource's access 'write'. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.flags` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.flags[].actions` | array | Preview |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.flags[].environments` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.flags[].ids` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.flags[].owners` | array | Preview |  |
| `auth.roles.*.label` | string | Stable | The role's name as people read it, wherever a screen names the role (accounts, grants, invitations). Absent: the id, made readable. Words only; it grants nothing. |
| `auth.roles.*.operations` | array | Stable | Operator reads over the authenticated App host: readiness, bundle (the sanitized support bundle) and workflows (the durable workflows room, with Cancel and Retry). In a suite's Console, for this App only: workflows, jobs (list and redrive), deliveries (event and webhook deliveries, list and redrive), stores (store layout status) and analytics (read-only). With the platform realm, support reads the support sessions of the role's own realm: a tenant role its own tenant's, a platform role every tenant's (the one view naming the operator); never granted by a feature. Independent of data and command grants. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.read` | boolean \| array | Stable | true grants the read ceiling (every declared resource); a list names some of them. Default `false`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.realm` | `"tenant"` · `"platform"` | Stable | The realm the role grants in: a tenant's (the default) or the platform realm's. Required on every role once auth.tenancy.platform is declared; a platform role edits only the platform's own writable resources, never the profile's New, and changes a tenant's rows only through its commands. One of `platform`, `tenant`. |
| `auth.roles.*.service` |  | Stable | A role only a service principal holds (a jobs module's principals, an App API token), never a person: a free-form page is offered to it only where the page names it; it is never defaultRole and has no claims. One of `true`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.roles.*.write` | boolean \| array | Stable | true grants the write ceiling (resources with access 'write'), within the role's reads. Default `false`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.rows` | `"all"` · `"policy"` · `"tenant"` | Stable | Row scoping: every row (default), a server-defined row policy (needs named sources), or tenant enrollment (exactly one named source). One of `all`, `policy`, `tenant`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |

| `auth.signUp` | string \| object | Stable | invite (default): an admin creates accounts. open: anyone may sign up. { providers, domains }: an account is made at its first sign-in through an identity provider, with a verified email in one of the domains. One of `invite`, `open`. |

## `auth.store`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.store` | string | Stable | Where accounts and sessions live: a SQLite file, or a postgres:// URL (name its password, or the whole URL, by a ${NAME} reference; migratePostgresAuthStore from @mistriwork/mistri/maintenance makes its schema before the first start). Never a business database, which a tenant App refuses at startup. Default: a SQLite file in the mistri config directory, named for the app. |

## `auth.tenancy`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.tenancy` | object | Stable | What one tenant is called, the platform-owned profile resource with one row per tenant, and the platform realm with its label. Only with auth.rows 'tenant'. |
| `auth.tenancy.label` | string | Stable | What one tenant is called in the chooser and the browser's own words ("Dealer"). |
| `auth.tenancy.platform` | object | Stable | Declares the platform realm, the business above the tenants. The server-only policy must then declare resolvePlatformRows. |
| `auth.tenancy.platform.label` | string | Stable | What the platform realm is called in the chooser ("Lender"). |
| `auth.tenancy.platform.me` | object | Stable | Who me is in the platform realm, as auth.me says it in a tenant's: the platform-owned resource its staff are rows of, and the column holding each one's account id, so a provider view can say owner_id = me. A tenant's member is never this row, and the platform's staff are never a tenant's person. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.tenancy.platform.me.column` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.tenancy.platform.me.from` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `auth.tenancy.profile` | string | Stable | The platform-owned resource with one row per tenant. A tenant's row may reference it, only through its ownership column. |
